quizzes.title: US Ties with Greenland: MCQ
quizzes.passage: Greenland is the world's largest island and one of two autonomous territories belonging to Denmark. Because Denmark is a member of NATO, Greenland is by default part of the North Atlantic Military Alliance. The island lies between North America and Europe, which places it at the centre of the security arrangements that link the two continents across the Arctic and the Atlantic. Greenland is described as a linchpin in Arctic and trans-Atlantic security architecture. Its location has also drawn sustained attention from the United States, and relations between Washington and Copenhagen over the island have a long history. Greenland's position also has a broader geostrategic dimension, since it sits between the Arctic and the Atlantic. Denmark's Prime Minister has rejected US claims about Greenland and reaffirmed Danish sovereignty over the territory. Greenland became a self-governing territory in 1979, and its colonial history began after an expedition led by Hans Egede arrived in 1721. Greenland has held the right to declare independence through a referendum since 2009. The island's strategic value rests on its geography, its history and its role in alliance security. For that reason, the island remains a subject of close interest to governments operating in the Arctic and the North Atlantic.

questions.q: During which war did the United States seize temporary control of Greenland?
questions.explanation: The booklet places the temporary US control of Greenland in World War II.

questions.q: The United States seized temporary control of Greenland to stop which country from exploiting the Danish colony?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the aim was to prevent Nazi Germany from exploiting the colony after Denmark's occupation.

questions.q: Greenland hosts critical infrastructure for which US system?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Greenland hosts critical infrastructure for the US Ballistic Missile Early-Warning System.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Greenland is considered an ideal location for ground stations that track polar-orbiting satellites.
Reason (R): Polar-orbiting satellites are essential for military intelligence and surveillance, GPS and navigation, and weather and climate monitoring.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements appear in the booklet, but the reason describes why the satellites matter, not why Greenland suits ground stations.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. 1946   ->   A. US offer of $100 million to Denmark for outright purchase of Greenland
II. 1951   ->   B. Defence agreement formalising American military access
III. GIUK Gap   ->   C. Key chokepoint for monitoring naval movements in the North Atlantic
IV. Pituffik Space Base   ->   D. Facility for monitoring potential missile threats
questions.explanation: Each item matches its booklet entry: the 1946 offer, the 1951 agreement, the GIUK chokepoint and the Pituffik monitoring base.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Greenland's strategic links:
I. Greenland enhances NATO's ability to monitor Russian activities in the Arctic and North Atlantic.
II. The 1951 defence agreement was signed between the United States and Russia.
III. The United States maintains Pituffik Space Base on Greenland.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The 1951 agreement was a US-Denmark arrangement, so only statements I and III are correct.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about Greenland are correct?
I. The US seized temporary control of Greenland during the Cold War.
II. Pituffik Space Base helps monitor potential missile threats from Russia, China and North Korea.
III. The 1951 defence agreement formalised American military access to Greenland.
questions.explanation: Statement I is wrong because the booklet places the seizure in World War II, so statements II and III are correct.

quizzes.title: US Ties with Greenland: Typed Answer
quizzes.passage: Greenland is the world's largest island and a self-governing territory of Denmark. Greenland is one of Denmark's two autonomous territories, alongside the Faroe Islands. Its history under Danish rule began in the early eighteenth century, when an expedition led by a Danish-Norwegian missionary arrived on the island. Greenland became a self-governing territory in 1979, and it has held the right to declare independence through a referendum since 2009. The island lies between North America and Europe, a position that makes it a linchpin in the security structure linking the two continents. Greenland is not a member state of the European Union, although it is associated with the bloc as one of its overseas countries and territories. Greenlanders are considered EU citizens under that association. Greenland joined the European Community together with Denmark in 1973 but left it in 1985, and the EU has since replaced that community. The island's location is considered ideal for ground stations. Greenland's strategic significance is also linked to its critical minerals and natural resources. Denmark has taken a firm stance on its sovereignty over the island, and Greenland's status shows how location, defence and sovereignty are tied together. Taken together, these features explain why the island has become a subject of international attention.

questions.q: In which year did the US propose a $100 million offer to Denmark for the outright purchase of Greenland?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the US proposal of a $100 million purchase offer to 1946.

questions.q: In which year was the US-Denmark Defence Agreement concluded?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the 1951 agreement formalised American military access to Greenland.

questions.q: Which type of satellites can Greenland's ground stations track? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Greenland is an ideal location for ground stations tracking polar-orbiting satellites.

questions.q: Which alliance's ability to monitor Russian activities in the Arctic and North Atlantic does Greenland enhance? (abbreviation)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Greenland enhances NATO's ability to monitor Russian activities.

questions.q: Which country currently maintains Pituffik Space Base? (short name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the US maintains Pituffik Space Base today.

questions.q: The Ballistic Missile Early-Warning System infrastructure in Greenland enables detection of what over the Arctic? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the infrastructure enables detection of missile launches over the Arctic.

questions.q: During which war did the US seize temporary control of Greenland? (standard name)
questions.explanation: The booklet places the US seizure of temporary control of Greenland in World War II.

quizzes.title: Great Power Competition and ACI: MCQ
quizzes.passage: The Arctic has become a region of growing interest for major powers. Melting ice is opening new maritime corridors, and control over these sea lanes will shape future global trade and naval power projection. The new routes could reduce travel time between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans, and they could lower fuel and shipping costs. Greenland lies between North America and Europe, within the Arctic and North Atlantic region, and it is described as a linchpin in Arctic and trans-Atlantic security architecture. Denmark is a member of NATO, so Greenland is by default part of the alliance. Greenland is one of Denmark's two autonomous territories, alongside the Faroe Islands. The island's untapped rare earth reserves are important for semiconductors, renewable energy technologies and defence systems. The European Union has a legal mechanism for situations in which a non-EU country pressures the bloc or its member states. The mechanism is designed for use when such pressure persists, and disputes are meant to be resolved through dialogue first. Escalation is considered only if necessary. Greenland joined the European Community together with Denmark in 1973 but left it in 1985, and the EU has since replaced that community. Greenlanders are considered EU citizens. Greenland is also the world's largest island and a self-governing territory of Denmark.

questions.q: Which country has heavily militarised its Arctic coastline?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Russia has heavily militarised its Arctic coastline.

questions.q: A French President urged the EU to invoke the Anti-Coercion Instrument for the first time against tariffs imposed by which country?
questions.explanation: The booklet links the French call to US tariffs during the Greenland dispute.

questions.q: Under the Anti-Coercion Instrument, a non-EU country's measures must affect which two areas for the EU to respond?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the instrument responds to measures that affect trade or investment.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Denmark takes a firm stance on sovereignty over Greenland.
Reason (R): The US views Greenland as central to countering both China and Russia.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements appear in the booklet, but the US view does not explain Denmark's stance.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Trade Measures   ->   A. Measures affecting intellectual property rights, public procurement and services
II. Investment Measures   ->   B. Restrictions on foreign direct investment
III. Market Access   ->   C. Import/export restrictions on goods and services
IV. IP & Services   ->   D. Limiting access to the EU internal market
questions.explanation: Each countermeasure in List I matches its booklet description in List II.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Greenland and the strategic environment:
I. China is investing in Arctic research and infrastructure.
II. The Anti-Coercion Instrument is primarily a tool for military retaliation.
III. Denmark's firm stance highlights tensions between territorial sovereignty and the strategic ambitions of major powers.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the booklet calls the instrument primarily a deterrent tool.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the EU's Anti-Coercion Instrument are correct?
I. Its objectives include protecting the EU's strategic autonomy.
II. It responds when a country within the EU coerces another EU member.
III. It aims to deter economic coercion.
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the booklet says the instrument responds to non-EU countries, so statements I and III are correct.

questions.q: Which country's President urged the EU to invoke the Anti-Coercion Instrument for the first time? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says a French President made this call.

questions.q: The Anti-Coercion Instrument is primarily a tool of what kind? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the instrument as primarily a deterrent tool.

questions.q: Which country has heavily militarised its Arctic coastline? (one word)

questions.q: Which country is investing in Arctic research and infrastructure? (one word)

questions.q: The Anti-Coercion Instrument aims to deter economic coercion and protect the EU's strategic ___ and policy space. (one word)

questions.q: What is the name of the countermeasure category covering restrictions on foreign direct investment? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Investment Measures as restrictions on foreign direct investment.

questions.q: Under the Anti-Coercion Instrument, what kind of response can be used if coercion persists? (two words)
